evals.prompt: With the Tasks API: list projects, then get a task for the first result.
evals.expected_output: Calls listProjects, then listTasks, then getTask in that order (as in examples/list-projects-to-get-task/), passing id -> projectId, ownerId -> assigneeId from listProjects's output into listTasks; never invents an id or path; validates arguments with validateArgs before each call.

evals.prompt: With the Tasks API, create a project using name "example-name".
evals.expected_output: Makes exactly one createProject call with arguments {"name":"example-name"} and nothing invented; POST /projects; reports the result.

evals.prompt: With the Tasks API, list labels in a project.
evals.expected_output: Does not guess projectId, which listLabels requires: gets it from listProjects (id -> projectId) or asks the user before calling listLabels; validateArgs would throw 'missing required argument "projectId"'.

evals.prompt: With the Tasks API, delete a comment (commentId "example-commentId").
evals.expected_output: Before deleteComment, says what it will delete or change and asks the user to confirm; calls deleteComment only after a yes, passing { confirmed: true } (the kit refuses "deleteComment is destructive" otherwise).

evals.prompt: With the Tasks API, edit a comment. I have not set up any credentials.
evals.expected_output: Notices TASKS_API_TOKEN is unset (buildRequest lists it in missingAuth; request refuses to send updateComment), asks the user to set it in the environment, and never invents, prints or commits a credential.

evals.prompt: With the Tasks API, list projects: all of them, not just the first page.
evals.expected_output: Calls listProjects repeatedly, passing cursor/limit from each response, until a page is empty or has no next cursor; reports how many items it read in total.

evals.prompt: With the Tasks API, email a summary of everything to my team.
evals.expected_output: Says plainly that none of the 22 operations in kit/operations.json can send email, does not fake it, and names the closest one, listProjects, offering to use it instead.
